name: bounded_state
one_line: A state schema with no field proportional to the horizon.
how_it_works: Carry five scalars, a mapping over a fixed account vocabulary, and a cursor naming the next shard.
The cursor replaces the list of what is left; the count replaces the list of what is done.
Everything else is identical to state_patch.
pros: Peak prompt moves from 949 bytes at 4 shards to 986 at 1,024. That is 37 bytes across a 256-fold increase in horizon.
One tenth the total bytes of state_patch at 1,024 shards: 1,000,925 against 10,409,501, for identical answers.
No horizon in reach. Nothing in the record grows with the input.
cons: Requires a closed vocabulary. The account mapping is bounded only because the accounts are known in advance.
The cursor imposes an order, so it cannot express work that jumps around or runs out of order.
Still one call per shard; it fixes bytes, not call count.
pick_this_when: The horizon is large or unbounded.
You can name a closed schema and prove no field grows with input.
avoid_when: You cannot bound the vocabulary. Then measure rather than assume.

evidence.finding: constant context is a property of the schema, not of the architecture
